>In article <1995Apr1...@omega.ntu.ac.sg> 740926...@omega.ntu.ac.sg (Damian Chang) writes:
>>If the chainsaw is to be corrected to a melee weapon, what about Talbot's
>>Chainsaw?

>Arghhh... I looked at my 2 Chainsaw's and 1 Shotgun in the first cards
>I've got, and concluded that Chainsaw /has to/ be a melee weapon ...
>until I heard about Talbot's. I'm confused.

>Maybe Chainsaw is alright and needs no fix; we just have to change the
>name of the /game/ to Jyhad: the Gathering (Vampire: the Ethernal Gathering
>for revised).

While chainsaws aren't melee weapons in real life (they do damage based on how
that chain goes 'rond the blade, not by how hard you hit with them - using
the game mechanics of "melee" weapon.), obviously the card is flawed.

Perhaps the text should be "once per round" rather than "once per combat".
Making it a melee weapon brings it into play at the cost of game concept,
which isn't necessarily a bad thing. But once per round makes more sense
for a weapon that you can't wield well (isn't balanced for fighting),
opposed to a one-shot weapon like a shotgun, which really does hold only
one shot (unless you have a fancy one, which Jyhad's obviously isn't).

You don't have to reload a chainsaw, just get it ready to strike again.
(Like an AD&D morning star, or a GURPS flail).

Either way would help balance the chainsaw so that it could make a
meaningful addition to a deck.

L. Scott

>come at you with a chainsaw: 1) Pee-Wee Herman

Cutting a tree at your leisure and *swinging* a chainsaw in combat are two
markedly different things. I wouldn't want either coming at me with a
chainsaw. Most of the damage from a chainsaw *strike* comes from the chain.
Just try dropping one of those thigs on your arm (as opposed to, say,
a bastard sword, and see which one does more damage from mere gravity).

Why can't Arnold use the chainsaw more than once in a combat?
